terms.meaning: The 19th century awakening under western ideas of science, humanism and rationalism, also called the Social and Religious Reformation.
The practice of a widow dying on her husband's pyre, declared illegal by William Bentinck in 1829.
Shraddananda's movement to bring converts back to Hinduism.
Brahmavidya Samaja, founded at New York in 1875 by Madame Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott.

items.name: Raja Ram Mohan Roy
items.formula: "Father of Indian Renaissance" (Tagore's words); founded Atmiya Sabha (1814) and Brahma Sabha (1828), renamed Brahma Samaj.
items.example: He opposed sati, caste, idol-worship and polygamy, and started the newspaper Samvada Kaumudi.

items.name: Prarthana Samaj (1867)
items.formula: Started by Atmaram Panduranga in Bombay; leaders M. G. Ranade and N. G. Chandavarkar.
items.example: It worked for widow marriage, intercaste marriage and women's uplift.

items.name: Jyotiba Phule and the Satya Shodak Samaj (1873)
items.formula: A non-Brahmin movement in Maharashtra; his book Gulamgiri (Slavery).
items.example: With Savitribai he opened a girls' school in Pune; Ambedkar saw him as his mentor.

items.name: Young Bengal Movement
items.formula: Led by Henri Vivian Derozio, who urged youth to think for themselves.

items.name: Arya Samaj (1875)
items.formula: Dayananda Saraswati (born Moolashankar): "Return to the Vedas"; his book Satyartha Prakasha.
items.example: Lala Hamsaraj set up the D.A.V. school in Lahore (1886).

items.name: Swami Vivekananda and the Ramakrishna Mission (1897)
items.formula: Born Narendranath Dutta on 12 January 1863, disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa; spoke at Chicago in 1893.
items.example: Tilak called him "The True Father of Indian Nationalism"; Chamarajendra Wodeyar X helped fund his trip.

items.name: Eshwarchandra Vidyasagar
items.formula: Opened a Sanskrit College for non-Brahmins.
items.example: He led the first legal upper-class widow remarriage in Kolkata in 1856.

items.name: Annie Besant and the Theosophists
items.formula: Their international office is at Adyar near Chennai; Besant set up the Central Hindu College (later BHU) and the Home Rule Movement.
items.example: She was the first woman President of the Congress (1917).

items.name: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and the Aligarh Movement
items.formula: Spread English education among Muslims; opposed purdah and polygamy; started the Aligarh Institute Gazette.
items.example: His Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College (1875) became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

items.name: Sri Narayana Guru
items.formula: Born in 1854 in an Ezhava family; founded the Sri Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam (1903).
items.example: "One God, One Religion and One Caste"; temples open to all.

items.name: Savitribai Phule
items.formula: Taught at the girls' school in Pune with her husband; ran a home for child widows.
items.example: She led the Satya Shodak Samaj after him and died nursing plague patients; Fatima Sheikh was her companion.

items.name: Tharabai Shinde
items.formula: Maharashtra's first woman freedom fighter, of the Satya Shodak Samaj.
items.example: Her book Stri Purush Tulana opposed the exploitation of women.

items.name: Panditha Ramabai
items.formula: A Christian reformer who founded the Mukti Mission in 1889.
items.example: It still shelters widows, orphans and alcoholics.

mistakes.text: Arya Samaj: Dayananda. Brahma Samaj: Roy. Prarthana Samaj: Atmaram Panduranga. Satya Shodak Samaj: Phule.
The Theosophical Society began in New York, not India; only its international office is at Adyar.
Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission and named it after his guru; Ramakrishna didn't found it.
